title: Rapid Scan Electron Paramagnetic Resonance Opens New Avenues for Imaging Physiologically Important Parameters In Vivo
protocol: Setup the Rapid Scan Coil Driver at 250 MHz.
Calculate the resonator bandwidth using vres and Q, where Q = 90 for the rapid scan resonator.
Determine the rapid scan rate allowed by the resonator bandwidth using N, ΔBpp, and a.
Select a conservative value for N between 5-6.
Use ΔBpp = 0.1 mT as a common value for radicals in representative results.
Set the signal bandwidth (BWsig) equal to the resonator bandwidth (BWRes).
Determine the maximum rapid scan frequency allowed by the rate.
Calculate the width of the scan to cover 100% of the spectrum using the determined value and the rate from Equation 2.
Use a sweep width of 7 mT for current probes used in vivo.
Determine the proper capacitance for the frequency using the inductance, L, of the rapid scan coils and Equation 4.
Divide CTOT obtained from Equation 4 in half to get the capacitor values for each side of the coil driver capacitor box.
Remove 15N-PDT from the freezer and allow it to reach room temperature (10-15 min).
Weigh out 1.4 mg of 15N-PDT using an analytical balance.
Add 1.4 mg of 15N-PDT to 15 ml de-ionized (DI) H2O for a final concentration of 0.5 mM.
Weigh out 0.7 mg of triaryl methyl radical (aTAM4) and dissolve in 200 µl of absolute ethanol.
Weigh 0.00681 g of KH2PO4 and dissolve in 50 ml DI water for a final concentration of 1 mM.
Weigh 2.8 g of KOH and dissolve in 50 ml of DI water for a final concentration of 1 M.
Add KOH drop wise to the phosphate buffer to adjust the pH to 7.0.
Add 800 µl of 1 mM phosphate buffer and 200 µl of aTAM4 in absolute ethanol for a final concentration of 0.5 mM in an 80:20 buffer:ethanol mixture.
Repeat steps to create the aTAM4 sample at pH = 7.2.
Place the aTAM4, pH=7.0 into a separate 6 mm quartz sample tube.
Place the aTAM4, pH=7.2 into another separate 6 mm quartz sample tube.
Place both 6 mm quartz EPR tubes into a 16 mm quartz EPR tube with a 2 mm thick Styrofoam spacer in between.
Weigh out 680 mg of KH2PO4 and dissolve in 100 ml DI water for a final concentration of 50 mM.
Add 1 M KOH drop wise to the phosphate buffer to pH=7.3.
Weigh out 50 mg of BMPO (199.25 g/mol).
Combine the 50 mg of BMPO with 5 ml of phosphate buffer in a 16 mm quartz irradiation tube.
Add 100 μl of 300 mM hydrogen peroxide to the mixture.
Irradiate the mixture in the 16 mm quartz irradiation tube with a medium pressure 450 W UV lamp for 5 min.
Using a glass transfer pipet, transfer 2.5 ml of irradiated BMPO-OH solution into one side of a 16 mm quartz sample tube with a 3 mm divider.
Transfer the remaining 2.5 ml of irradiated BMPO-OH into the other side of the 16 mm quartz sample tube with a 3 mm divider.
Weigh out 24.7 mg of 2H,15N-disulfide dinitroxide in 1 ml DMSO for a stock solution of 47.5 mM.
Prepare 10 mM Tris buffer and adjust to pH 7.2.
Take 40 μl dinitroxide stock solution and dilute with Tris buffer to a final concentration of 1 mM.
Place 250 μl of dinitroxide solution in buffer in a 16 mm quartz sample tube with a 10 mm divider in the center.
Weigh out 154 mg of glutathione and add to 5 ml of Tris buffer for a final concentration of 100 mM.
Add 5 μl of the 100 mM glutathione solution to 250 μl of 1 mM dinitroxide solution on one side of the 10 mm divider to convert the diradical into monoradical.
Remove nitronyl nitroxide from the freezer and allow it to come to room temperature (10-15 min).
Weigh out 1.9 mg of nitronyl (390 g/mol) and dissolve in 10 ml DI water with 0.56 mg KOH for a final concentration of 1 mM.
Mix the 1.9 mg of nitronyl into 10 ml of 1 mM KOH solution for a final concentration of 0.5 mM nitronyl.
Tune the resonator with an aqueous sample of nitroxide radical.
Insert 15 ml of 0.5 mM 15N-PDT in water sample into a 16 mm quartz EPR tube.
Insert the quartz tube into the detection side of the cross-loop RS-EPR resonator.
Change the frequency of the instrument source to match the frequency of the detection side.
Manually change the carrier frequency of the 250 MHz source via software.
Adjust the excitation side frequency to match the experiment source and detection side frequencies.
Turn a variable capacitor within the resonator cavity according to manufacturer's protocol.
Set up Instrument Console and Main Magnet.
Turn on the spectrometer and choose an experiment that records transient data with time on the abscissa.
Within the software, set the number of points to 65,536 and the time base to 10 nsec.
Set the number of averages to 10,000 for a strong or narrow signal, and to 45,000 for a broad or weak signal.
Press the "engage" button in the software to send parameters from the software to the console and energize the main field magnet.
Set the main magnetic field to 9 mT.
Set the power attenuation knob to 50 dB.
Turn on the 7 W high power amplifier.
Turn on the rapid scan coil driver with specified values.
Collect a rapid scan spectrum starting at 50 dB with 100k averages.
Decrease the attenuation by 3 dB and repeat measurement until isolation measurement on bridge readout is less than 0 or attenuator setting reaches 0 dB.
Transfer raw rapid scan data into deconvolution program.
Process raw data into absorption spectrum using specified parameters in program.
Plot amplitude of absorption signal as a function of square root power incident on resonator.
Fit trend line starting at 0,0 and include all data points within linear response region for analysis.
